wins.text: Worldwide Q1 sales of $21.9B, up 4.2% operationally despite ~810 bps STELARA biosimilar headwind in Innovative Medicine; ex-STELARA, remaining ~90% of IM business grew over 12% with 11 key brands growing double digits

DARZALEX delivered 22.5% growth with ~3 pts share gains across all lines and ~5 pts in frontline; CARVYKTI grew over 100% YoY to $369M with 10.5% sequential growth; RYBREVANT+LAZCLUZE grew over 100% to $141M

TREMFYA grew 20.1% operationally, achieving nearly $1B in sales; already captured ~50% share of IL-23 new patient starts in UC; Crohn's disease launch patient initiation volumes outpacing prior IL-23 launches

Full-year operational sales guidance raised by $700M to midpoint of $92B (3.8% growth) following Intra-Cellular/CAPLYTA acquisition close; adjusted EPS guidance maintained at $10.50–$10.70 midpoint despite $0.25 Intra-Cellular dilution and tariff headwinds
63rd consecutive annual dividend increase announced at 4.8%; free cash flow of ~$3.4B in Q1; $7B talc reserve reversal boosted reported net earnings to $11B and EPS to $4.54

risks.text: Tariff exposure estimated at ~$400M in 2025, primarily MedTech-driven (China retaliatory tariffs on U.S.-origin products most penalizing); full-year annualized impact deliberately not quantified due to fluidity; limited pricing power to pass through costs given contractual agreements and pharma pricing constraints
Gross margins compressed ~320 bps YoY driven by STELARA mix headwind, Part D redesign, and unfavorable transactional currency; management acknowledged consensus was too optimistic on gross profit

Orthopedics declined 3.1% with underlying competitive pressure in Spine and Sports; hips and knees performance described as 'slightly below market' in Q1; Surgery restructuring program expected to cause ~$250M revenue disruption over next 2 years at ~$900M cost
STELARA biosimilar erosion expected to accelerate throughout 2025 following HUMIRA erosion curve, compounded by Part D redesign; STELARA declined 32.3% in Q1 with further acceleration anticipated

Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff investigation ongoing; potential for broader pharma tariffs creates supply chain and cost uncertainty; management declined to discuss transfer pricing structures for competitive reasons

guidance_items.detail: Full-year operational sales growth raised to 3.3%–4.3% (midpoint $92B) from prior range, adding $700M for CAPLYTA/Intra-Cellular; reported sales growth 2.6%–3.6% (midpoint $91.4B) reflecting improved FX of +$1.1B vs prior guide
Adjusted diluted EPS maintained at $10.50–$10.70 (6.2% growth at midpoint) despite $0.25 Intra-Cellular dilution and ~$400M tariff headwind, aided by reduced FX drag
Operating margin improvement of 300 bps vs 2024 maintained, inclusive of Intra-Cellular dilution and known tariff impacts
Net interest expense guided to $100M–$200M (vs prior guide), reflecting Intra-Cellular financing costs; Other income guided to $1.0B–$1.2B, slight increase vs prior

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Full annualized tariff impact and transfer pricing structure exposure under Section 232 pharma tariff investigation
Orthopedics competitive share loss in hips/knees being below market, independent of one-time items
Recession risk and potential demand softness for elective procedures
